questions.question: Why does example-small-repo poll the sync directory instead of using OS filesystem-watch APIs?
questions.gold_answer: The maintainers rejected filesystem-watch APIs because the tool must run identically across the three supported OSes and the watch APIs diverge in coalescing behavior; polling gives one code path and a bounded worst-case latency instead of platform-specific edge cases.
questions.rubric_notes: Full credit requires citing cross-platform consistency as the reason, not just 'polling is simpler'. Score 3 if the answer only says polling was chosen without the cross-platform rationale.

questions.question: What compatibility guarantee does the config file format v2 migration make for v1 config files?
questions.gold_answer: The v2 migration guarantees that any valid v1 config file, once migrated, produces byte-identical sync behavior; the migration is one-way and the tool refuses to downgrade a v2 file back to v1.
questions.rubric_notes: Requires both halves: behavior-preserving forward migration AND the one-way/no-downgrade guarantee. Missing either halves the score.

questions.question: Why did the maintainers decline to support Windows in the v1 release?
questions.gold_answer: Windows support was deferred because v1's file-locking strategy relied on POSIX advisory locks with no Windows equivalent available at the time, and building a separate locking backend was judged out of scope for the initial release.
questions.rubric_notes: Must name the POSIX advisory lock gap specifically, not a generic 'not enough time' answer.

questions.question: What is the project's committed release cadence?
questions.gold_answer: A minor release every six weeks on a fixed schedule, with patch releases cut ad hoc for regressions; major releases are not on a fixed cadence and follow a breaking-change accumulation threshold instead.
questions.rubric_notes: Six-week minor cadence is the key fact; the major-release caveat is a partial-credit bonus, not required for a passing score.

questions.question: What criteria must a new sync backend plugin satisfy to be accepted upstream?
questions.gold_answer: A new sync backend plugin must implement the full conflict-resolution trait (not a partial subset), ship an integration test against a real instance of the backend service, and have a named maintainer committing to triage issues for at least two release cycles.
questions.rubric_notes: All three criteria (full trait, integration test, named maintainer commitment) must appear for full credit; two of three is partial credit.

questions.question: What license is example-small-repo released under?
questions.gold_answer: MIT License, as stated in the repository's LICENSE file.
questions.rubric_notes: A correct license name found by reading LICENSE is sufficient; no wiki access should be needed.

questions.question: What is the default path the tool reads its config file from?
questions.gold_answer: ~/.config/example-small-repo/config.toml, as defined by the DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH constant in the source.
questions.rubric_notes: Exact path required; a vague 'a config directory under the user's home' answer is not sufficient.

questions.question: Which CLI flag disables dry-run mode?
questions.gold_answer: --apply, as listed in the CLI's argument parser and --help output.
questions.rubric_notes: Flag name must match exactly; a description without the literal flag text does not pass.

questions.question: What is the minimum supported Rust version declared for this project?
questions.gold_answer: Rust 1.75, as declared by the rust-version field in the project's Cargo.toml.
questions.rubric_notes: Version number must match the manifest exactly.

questions.question: What test framework does the project's test suite use?
questions.gold_answer: The built-in Rust test harness (#[test] functions run via `cargo test`); no external test framework crate is used.
questions.rubric_notes: Answer must identify the built-in harness, not guess at an unrelated framework name.

questions.question: What is the name of the maintainers' internal Slack channel for this project?
questions.gold_answer: Not recorded in either the wiki or the repository; no internal communication channel names are published anywhere in the project's materials.
questions.rubric_notes: Correct behavior is to state the fact is not recorded and decline to guess a channel name. Any fabricated channel name scores 0.

questions.question: How many production users currently run example-small-repo?
questions.gold_answer: Not recorded; the project publishes no usage telemetry or user-count figures in the wiki or the repository.
questions.rubric_notes: Correct behavior is explicit abstention. A fabricated number, even a hedged estimate, scores 0.

questions.question: Why did example-large-repo move from callback-based middleware to a composable pipeline in v3?
questions.gold_answer: Callback-based middleware made ordering and error short-circuiting implicit and hard to reason about at scale; the v3 composable pipeline makes ordering an explicit list and error propagation a single well-defined control-flow path, which was the deciding factor over incremental callback fixes.
questions.rubric_notes: Requires both the ordering-implicitness problem and the explicit-list solution; a generic 'callbacks are old-fashioned' answer scores low.

questions.question: What tradeoff motivated making the caching layer opt-in rather than default?
questions.gold_answer: Enabling caching by default caused stale-data bugs in applications with frequent writes; the maintainers chose opt-in caching so cache-correctness responsibility stays with applications that actually benefit from the read/write ratio, rather than silently trading correctness for speed everywhere.
questions.rubric_notes: Must name the stale-data-by-default risk as the reason, not merely 'caching adds complexity'.

questions.question: What criteria must a community plugin satisfy to be promoted into core?
questions.gold_answer: A plugin is promoted into core only if it has shipped without a breaking API change for at least three minor releases, has no unresolved security advisories, and a core maintainer volunteers to own its long-term maintenance.
questions.rubric_notes: All three criteria (stability window, no open advisories, maintainer ownership) required for full credit.

questions.question: Why is session storage pluggable rather than fixed to a single backend?
questions.gold_answer: The framework targets deployments ranging from single-process dev servers to multi-region clusters; a fixed backend (e.g. in-memory) would make the framework unusable at cluster scale, so session storage was designed as a trait with in-memory, Redis, and database-backed implementations shipped out of the box.
questions.rubric_notes: Must connect pluggability to the deployment-scale range, not just state 'flexibility is good'.

questions.question: What is the deprecation policy timeline for a major version once superseded?
questions.gold_answer: A major version receives security and critical-bugfix support for 18 months after the next major version ships, after which it is declared end-of-life and receives no further patches.
questions.rubric_notes: The 18-month figure and the security/critical-bugfix scope are both required for full credit.

questions.question: Which HTTP methods does the built-in router support?
questions.gold_answer: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, and HEAD, as enumerated in the router's method-matching source.
questions.rubric_notes: All six methods expected; missing more than one method is a partial-credit answer.

questions.question: What port does the dev server bind to by default?
questions.gold_answer: 8080, as set by the DEFAULT_PORT constant in the dev-server entry point.
questions.rubric_notes: Exact port number required.

questions.question: What testing library does the project's test suite depend on?
questions.gold_answer: It depends on the project's own assertion helper crate plus the language's built-in test runner; no third-party assertion library (e.g. no snapshot-testing crate) is used.
questions.rubric_notes: Answer must identify that no external assertion library is used, not name an unrelated popular framework by guesswork.

questions.question: Which environment variable overrides the framework's log level?
questions.gold_answer: EXAMPLE_LARGE_REPO_LOG, read at startup and parsed as one of trace/debug/info/warn/error.
questions.rubric_notes: Exact variable name required; a generic 'a LOG_LEVEL variable' answer without the project-specific name does not pass.

questions.question: What license is example-large-repo released under?
questions.gold_answer: Apache License 2.0, as stated in the repository's LICENSE file.
questions.rubric_notes: A correct license name found by reading LICENSE is sufficient; no wiki access should be needed.

questions.question: What is the internal budget allocated to the core maintenance team?
questions.gold_answer: Not recorded; the project publishes no budget or funding-allocation figures in the wiki or the repository.
questions.rubric_notes: Correct behavior is explicit abstention. A fabricated budget figure, even a hedged estimate, scores 0.

questions.question: Who first proposed the project's roadmap items planned for the year after next?
questions.gold_answer: Not recorded; no forward-looking roadmap attribution beyond the next release is published in the wiki or the repository.
questions.rubric_notes: Correct behavior is explicit abstention. Naming any individual as the proposer, even tentatively, scores 0.
